# EntropyError

Why unpredictable bytes could not be obtained.

```rux
pub enum EntropyError {
    Unsupported,
    Interrupted,
    Failed,
    TooLarge
}
```

Every case is a failure: nothing was written that a caller may rely on. A filled buffer is the success channel of
the `! EntropyError` the fill returns.

## Cases

| Name          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Unsupported` | This system has no entropy source this package can reach. A kernel too old for its own generator reports this. It does not change while a program runs, so retrying is pointless.          |
| `Interrupted` | The source kept being interrupted, and the call gave up rather than looping forever. Ordinary on a process taking signals steadily. Worth one more attempt; not worth an unbounded number. |
| `Failed`      | The source refused for a reason the system did not make actionable.                                                                                                                        |
| `TooLarge`    | The request was larger than the source accepts in one call. Windows takes a 32-bit count, so a request above four gigabytes has no honest answer. Split it.                                |

## Methods

<h3 id="is-transient"><code>IsTransient</code></h3>

```rux
pub func IsTransient(self: *EntropyError) -> bool
```

Whether trying again might work.
`self` is borrowed. True for `Interrupted`, which says a signal arrived rather than that anything is wrong.
False for everything else: a system with no source will not grow one, and a refusal repeated is still a
refusal.
Cannot fail. Runs in constant time and allocates nothing.

**Returns**: whether asking again could succeed
